title: Metals and Alloys
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Real objects: a copper wire, a mabati offcut, a brass padlock or tap, a steel spoon, an aluminium sufuria. The rusting test (three nails in three conditions) runs for a week. Learners never handle acids for galvanising; it is described.

skills.key_step: The child names the physical properties of metals (shiny, good conductors of heat and electricity, malleable, ductile, strong, mostly solid with high melting points) and links each use to the property it needs.
representations: a property chart with an object for each
steps: Conduct heat: sufurias; conduct electricity: wires.
Match the use to the property.

board.do: Draw a wire, a sufuria and a sheet of mabati.

board.say: Which property let it be made into a thin sheet?

board.do: Ask the child to write the property beside the other two.

misconceptions.ask: Does foil shine, bend and conduct?

checks.question: Why are sufurias made of aluminium?
checks.answer: it conducts heat well and is light

skills.key_step: The child says an alloy is a mixture of a metal with other elements, names brass (copper and zinc), bronze (copper and tin) and steel (iron with a little carbon), and says alloys are made to be harder, stronger or last longer.

floor.question: Is a mixture made of one substance or more?

representations: a brass tap, a steel spoon, a bronze medal picture
a chart: alloy, made of, use
a soft iron nail and a steel spoon to bend
steps: An alloy is a mixture with a metal.
contexts: steel rods on a building site

board.do: Draw a table: alloy, made of, use.
Ask the child to fill in bronze.

misconceptions.ask: What is added to iron to make steel?
Which is copper and tin: brass or bronze?
Can an alloy contain a non-metal?
misconceptions.repair: Steel is iron with a little carbon.

misconceptions.ask: Which bent more easily: the iron nail or the steel spoon?
misconceptions.repair: Alloys are made to be stronger.

checks.question: What is an alloy?
checks.answer: a mixture of a metal with other elements

checks.question: Name the alloy made of copper and zinc.

skills.key_step: The child says rusting is iron reacting with oxygen and water, that it weakens iron and steel, and that painting, oiling, greasing, galvanising and plating prevent it by keeping air and water away.

floor.prerequisite: Knows a chemical change makes a new substance.
floor.question: Is rusting a physical or chemical change?

representations: three nails: dry air, boiled water under oil, air and water
a painted and an unpainted iron sheet
a chart: method, how it keeps air or water away
steps: Rust flakes and weakens the metal.
Keep air or water away: paint, oil, grease.
Coat with zinc (galvanising) or another metal (plating).

board.do: Draw three test tubes with nails: dry, water with oil on top, open water.

misconceptions.ask: Why did the nail under oil not rust?
misconceptions.repair: Iron needs air and water to rust.
Paint or oil keeps air and water away.

misconceptions.ask: What happens to a nail when rust flakes off?
Which old pot went brown and flaky?

checks.question: What two things does iron need to rust?
Give one way to prevent a bicycle chain rusting.
